reference.title: Red Hat Quay new features and enhancements
reference.shortdesc: You can review new features and enhancements in Red Hat Quay 3.18, including multi-issuer OIDC support, programmatic OAuth token provisioning, and OAuth API access tokens in the UI.

section.title: Microsoft Entra ID v2 token and multi-issuer OIDC support
section.p: With this release, Red Hat Quay supports multiple OIDC issuers and audiences per identity provider in *_LOGIN_CONFIG blocks. You can configure Red Hat Quay to accept Microsoft Entra ID v1.0 and v2.0 tokens from the same provider, validate custom token audiences for On-Behalf-Of (OBO) API flows, and optionally restrict which client applications can authenticate by using the authorized party (azp) claim.

This enhancement enables integrations with Red Hat Developer Hub (RHDH), Red Hat Dev Spaces, and other tools that use modern Entra ID v2.0 access tokens. Existing configurations that use a single OIDC_ISSUER continue to work without changes.
Red Hat Quay now validates token audiences on API bearer-token requests. Audience verification is no longer disabled for SSO bearer tokens.

Federated robot authentication also supports an optional audiences array on each federation configuration entry. When configured, Red Hat Quay validates the external OIDC token audience during robot token exchange. When absent, audience validation is skipped and a deprecation warning is logged. For more information, see Robot federation audiences field.
For configuration field descriptions, see OIDC multi-issuer configuration fields. For setup and migration procedures, see Configuring Microsoft Entra ID v2 and multi-issuer OIDC.

section.title: Programmatic OAuth token provisioning (Tech Preview)
section.p: Red Hat Quay 3.18 introduces programmatic OAuth API token life cycle management for organization applications. You can create, list, and revoke OAuth API tokens by using the REST API instead of the UI.

When FEATURE_PROGRAMMATIC_BOOTSTRAP is enabled, Red Hat Quay can also auto-generate a high-privilege bootstrap OAuth token on startup and write it to a local file or Kubernetes Secret. Use this bootstrap token for zero-touch automation workflows such as GitOps-based deployments, CI/CD bootstrap, and headless registry provisioning.
This feature is available as Tech Preview in Red Hat Quay 3.18.
For configuration fields, see Programmatic bootstrap configuration fields. For setup and examples, see Programmatic OAuth token provisioning.

section.title: OAuth API Access Tokens management UI
section.p: With this release, organization OAuth applications include an API Access Tokens page in the Red Hat Quay v2 UI. You can create named OAuth 2 access tokens, review token metadata such as scopes and last-used time, delete individual tokens, and rotate legacy long-lived (10 years) tokens without deleting the parent OAuth application.
Existing tokens continue to work for up to 10 years until you revoke them.
For more information, see Creating an OAuth 2 access token and Rotating a legacy OAuth 2 access token.

section.title: Repository mirror metrics and health monitoring
section.p: Red Hat Quay 3.18 adds Prometheus metrics and a health API endpoint for repository mirroring. Operators can monitor synchronization status, pending tags, and failures per repository and set up alerts in Prometheus or Grafana.
Four new per-repository metrics are available from the mirror worker metrics endpoint:

ul.li: quay_repository_mirror_last_sync_status — last sync outcome (failed, success, or in progress)
quay_repository_mirror_sync_complete — whether all tags synchronized in the last run
quay_repository_mirror_sync_failures_total — cumulative failure count by namespace and reason

section.p: For more information, see Monitoring repository mirroring, getRepositoryMirrorHealth, and getSuperUserRepositoryMirrorHealth.
